The image depicts the Java compilation and execution process. A .java file is fed into the Java Compiler (javac), which compiles it into a .class file. This .class file is then loaded by the Class Loader, which is a component of the Java Virtual Machine (JVM). The loaded bytecode is then verified by the Bytecode Verifier, another component of the JVM, to ensure its integrity and security. Finally, the Java Runtime System within the JVM executes the verified bytecode, interacting with the Native OS as needed.

Parse tree shows the derivation of the expression where expr is the root node with term and term as children, the left term has + as a child, + has factor and factor as children, the first factor has * as a child and * has factor as a child, and the second factor has 7 as a child, and the factor has 3 as a child, the leftmost factor has 2 as a child.

The image depicts a compilation process with three stages starting with an input source code on a computer screen labeled “Symbol (! ‘!”)”. Stage one is Lexical Analysis, transforming the input into a series of tokens represented by stacked boxes. Stage two is Syntax Analysis, building an Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) from those tokens. The AST is a hierarchical representation of the code's structure. Finally, Stage three is Code Generation, visualizing code being built by a crane with the final output of “!”. The bottom text labels the input as “input” and the stacked boxes as “tokens”, and the tree is labeled “AST”.
